title: Gatchalian: P7.2 trillion 2027 budget ratified by December 17
summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian yesterday ruled out a reenacted budget for 2027, warning that the country’s sluggish economy cannot afford delays in passing the proposed P7.2-trillion…

blocks.text: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian delivered his address in the opening of the 2nd regular session of the Senate, July 27, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian yesterday ruled out a reenacted budget for 2027, warning that the country’s sluggish economy cannot afford delays in passing the proposed P7.2-trillion national spending plan.

Speaking with radio dzBB, Gatchalian stressed that the chamber is racing to ratify the 2027 General Appropriations Bill before Congress adjourns in mid-December, even as senators juggle the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and dozens of pending presidential appointments.
“For us, a reenacted budget is not an option because our economy is bad. We need a fresh and new budget so that our economy will move faster,” he said.
The Senate is set to open plenary debates on the budget today, with senators bracing for late-night sessions to wrap up deliberations within two weeks.

Under the timetable discussed with Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito, the chamber targets holding the bicameral conference committee around the week of Dec. 13 and ratifying the final bill before Dec. 17 so it can be transmitted to Malacañang for President Marcos’ signature.

Gatchalian said senators are prepared to sacrifice their holiday breaks should a deadlock arise with the House of Representatives, recalling how last year’s impasse pushed budget ratification to nearly Dec. 29.

Compounding the tight calendar is the Commission on Appointments (CA), which must process before the Dec. 17 adjournment roughly 35 presidential appointees, including Cabinet secretaries, ambassadors, and military officers facing birthday age-limit cutoffs for promotion, to prevent them from being bypassed.
To manage the workload, the CA will hold three hearings before the break, starting at 8 a.m. today before giving way to plenary budget debates at 1 p.m.

Meanwhile, Gatchalian noted that while senators aim to conclude Duterte’s impeachment trial before yearend, the timeline remains flexible depending on the remaining six defense witnesses and the length of questioning by prosecutors and senator-judges.
“No matter the verdict, conviction or acquittal, the consensus is for this (trial) to conclude before yearend,” he said.
